sanskrit: tasmāt pānīyadānād vai na paraṃ vidyate kva cit tac ca dadyān naro nityaṃ ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ
english: Therefore nowhere is there a gift higher than the giving of water; and the man who would seek his own well-being should give it without ceasing.

sanskrit: dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ jaladānaṃ viśāṃ pate śatrūṃś cāpy adhi kaunteya sadā tiṣṭhati toyadaḥ
english: The giving of water brings fortune, fame, and length of days, O lord of peoples; and the giver of water, O son of Kuntī, stands ever superior even to his enemies.

sanskrit: sarvakāmān avāpnoti kīrtiṃ caiveha śāśvatīm pretya cānantyam āpnoti pāpebhyaś ca pramucyate
english: He gains all his desires and undying renown in this world; after death he attains the endless realms and is set free from his sins.

sanskrit: toyado manujavyāghra svargaṃ gatvā mahādyute akṣayān samavāpnoti lokān ity abravīn manuḥ
english: The giver of water, O tiger among men, O greatly resplendent one, having gone to heaven, attains the imperishable worlds — so said Manu.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tilānāṃ kīdṛśaṃ dānam atha dīpasya caiva ha annānāṃ vāsasāṃ caiva bhūya eva bravīhi me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what kind is the gift of sesame seeds, and of lamps as well, and of food and of garments? Tell me of these once again.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam brāhmaṇasya ca saṃvādaṃ yamasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue of a brāhmaṇa and Yama, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: madhyadeśe mahān grāmo brāhmaṇānāṃ babhūva ha gaṅgāyamunayor madhye yāmunasya girer adhaḥ
english: In the Middle Country there was once a great village of brāhmaṇas, set between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, below the Yāmuna mountain.

sanskrit: parṇaśāleti vikhyāto ramaṇīyo narādhipa vidvāṃsas tatra bhūyiṣṭhā brāhmaṇāś cāvasaṃs tadā
english: It was renowned as Parṇaśālā and was a place of delight, O ruler of men; and learned brāhmaṇas in great numbers dwelt there in those days.

sanskrit: atha prāha yamaḥ kaṃ cit puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇavāsasam raktākṣam ūrdhvaromāṇaṃ kākajaṅghākṣināsikam
english: Then Yama spoke to a certain man clad in black garments, red-eyed, with hair standing on end, with the shanks, eyes, and nose of a crow.

sanskrit: gaccha tvaṃ brāhmaṇagrāmaṃ tato gatvā tam ānaya agastyaṃ gotrataś cāpi nāmataś cāpi śarmiṇam
english: "Go you to the village of the brāhmaṇas, and going there bring back the one of the Agastya line by gotra, and Śarman by name.

sanskrit: śame niviṣṭaṃ vidvāṃsam adhyāpakam anādṛtam mā cānyam ānayethās tvaṃ sagotraṃ tasya pārśvataḥ
english: He is settled in tranquillity, learned, a teacher, yet little honored; and do not bring back another of his same gotra dwelling beside him.

sanskrit: sa hi tādṛgguṇas tena tulyo 'dhyayanajanmanā apatyeṣu tathā vṛtte samastenaiva dhīmatā tam ānaya yathoddiṣṭaṃ pūjā kāryā hi tasya me
english: For that other one is of like qualities, equal to him in study and in birth, in offspring, and in conduct — wholly his match in wisdom. Bring back the one I have appointed, for I must do him honor."

sanskrit: sa gatvā pratikūlaṃ tac cakāra yamaśāsanam tam ākramyānayām āsa pratiṣiddho yamena yaḥ
english: He went and did the contrary to Yama's command: he seized and brought back the very one whom Yama had forbidden.

sanskrit: tasmai yamaḥ samutthāya pūjāṃ kṛtvā ca vīryavān provāca nīyatām eṣa so 'nya ānīyatām iti
english: To him the mighty Yama rose up and did honor, then declared, "Let this man be taken back, and let that other be brought instead."

sanskrit: evam ukte tu vacane dharmarājena sa dvijaḥ uvāca dharmarājānaṃ nirviṇṇo 'dhyayanena vai yo me kālo bhavec cheṣas taṃ vaseyam ihācyuta
english: When the King of Righteousness had spoken thus, that twice-born one, weary of his studies, said to the Dharmarāja: "Whatever span of life remains to me, let me dwell it out here, O imperishable one."

sanskrit: yama uvāca nāhaṃ kālasya vihitaṃ prāpnomīha kathaṃ cana yo hi dharmaṃ carati vai taṃ tu jānāmi kevalam
english: Yama said: "In no way can I overstep what Time has ordained; I only know who it is that practices righteousness.

sanskrit: gaccha vipra tvam adyaiva ālayaṃ svaṃ mahādyute brūhi vā tvaṃ yathā svairaṃ karavāṇi kim ity uta
english: Go, brāhmaṇa, this very day to your own home, O greatly resplendent one; or speak as you freely wish — what shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca yat tatra kṛtvā sumahat puṇyaṃ syāt tad bravīhi me sarvasya hi pramāṇaṃ tvaṃ trailokyasyāpi sattama
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "Tell me that deed which, done back there, would bring the greatest merit; for you are the standard of all, even of the three worlds, O most excellent one."

sanskrit: yama uvāca śṛṇu tattvena viprarṣe pradānavidhim uttamam tilāḥ paramakaṃ dānaṃ puṇyaṃ caiveha śāśvatam
english: Yama said: "Hear truly, O sage among brāhmaṇas, the supreme rule of giving. Sesame seeds are the highest gift, and their merit here is everlasting.

sanskrit: tilāś ca saṃpradātavyā yathāśakti dvijarṣabha nityadānāt sarvakāmāṃs tilā nirvartayanty uta
english: Sesame seeds should be given according to one's power, O bull among the twice-born; given without ceasing, sesame fulfills every desire.

sanskrit: tilāñ śrāddhe praśaṃsanti dānam etad dhy anuttamam tān prayacchasva viprebhyo vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: They praise sesame at the rites for the ancestors, for this gift is unsurpassed; bestow it upon the brāhmaṇas with rites performed as the ordinance directs.

sanskrit: tilā bhakṣayitavyāś ca sadā tv ālabhanaṃ ca taiḥ kāryaṃ satatam icchadbhiḥ śreyaḥ sarvātmanā gṛhe
english: Sesame should be eaten always, and with it the touching of the body should be performed without fail by those who, with their whole heart, desire well-being in the home.

sanskrit: tathāpaḥ sarvadā deyāḥ peyāś caiva na saṃśayaḥ puṣkariṇyas taḍāgāni kūpāṃś caivātra khānayet
english: So too water should ever be given and offered to drink — of this there is no doubt; and here one should have lotus-pools, tanks, and wells dug out.

sanskrit: etat sudurlabhataram iha loke dvijottama āpo nityaṃ pradeyās te puṇyaṃ hy etad anuttamam
english: This is the rarest of all in the world, O best of the twice-born; water should ever be given by you, for this merit is unsurpassed.

sanskrit: prapāś ca kāryāḥ pānārthaṃ nityaṃ te dvijasattama bhukte 'py atha pradeyaṃ te pānīyaṃ vai viśeṣataḥ
english: And watering-sheds should ever be built by you for men to drink, O most excellent of the twice-born; and even after a meal you should especially offer water to drink."

sanskrit: ity ukte sa tadā tena yamadūtena vai gṛhān nītaś cakāra ca tathā sarvaṃ tad yamaśāsanam
english: When this had been spoken, he was then led home by that messenger of Yama, and he carried out in full all that command of Yama.

sanskrit: nītvā taṃ yamadūto 'pi gṛhītvā śarmiṇaṃ tadā yayau sa dharmarājāya nyavedayata cāpi tam
english: Having brought that man home, the messenger of Yama then took Śarman and went, and presented him to the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: taṃ dharmarājo dharmajñaṃ pūjayitvā pratāpavān kṛtvā ca saṃvidaṃ tena visasarja yathāgatam
english: The majestic King of Righteousness honored that knower of dharma, and having made his compact with him, sent him back as he had come.

sanskrit: tasyāpi ca yamaḥ sarvam upadeśaṃ cakāra ha pratyetya ca sa tat sarvaṃ cakāroktaṃ yamena tat
english: To him too Yama gave the whole instruction; and returning, that man did all that Yama had told.

sanskrit: tathā praśaṃsate dīpān yamaḥ pitṛhitepsayā tasmād dīpaprado nityaṃ saṃtārayati vai pitṝn
english: Likewise Yama praises lamps, desiring the welfare of the ancestors; therefore the giver of lamps forever carries the fathers across.

sanskrit: dātavyāḥ satataṃ dīpās tasmād bharatasattama devānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ca cakṣuṣy āste matāḥ prabho
english: Lamps should be given always, O most excellent of the Bharatas; for they are held to abide in the eyes of the gods and of the fathers, O lord.

sanskrit: ratnadānaṃ ca sumahat puṇyam uktaṃ janādhipa tāni vikrīya yajate brāhmaṇo hy abhayaṃkaraḥ
english: The gift of gems too is declared a very great merit, O ruler of men; for selling them, the brāhmaṇa, the giver of safety, performs sacrifice.

sanskrit: yad vai dadāti viprebhyo brāhmaṇaḥ pratigṛhya vai ubhayoḥ syāt tad akṣayyaṃ dātur ādātur eva ca
english: Whatever a brāhmaṇa, having himself received, gives to other brāhmaṇas becomes imperishable for both — for the giver and for the receiver alike.

sanskrit: yo dadāti sthitaḥ sthityāṃ tādṛśāya pratigraham ubhayor akṣayaṃ dharmaṃ taṃ manuḥ prāha dharmavit
english: He who, abiding in right conduct, gives a gift to be received by such a man — this Manu, the knower of dharma, declared an imperishable merit for both.

sanskrit: vāsasāṃ tu pradānena svadāranirato naraḥ suvastraś ca suveṣaś ca bhavatīty anuśuśruma
english: By the gift of garments, a man devoted to his own wife becomes well-clothed and well-adorned — so have we heard in turn.

sanskrit: gāvaḥ suvarṇaṃ ca tathā tilāś caivānuvarṇitāḥ bahuśaḥ puruṣavyāghra vedaprāmāṇyadarśanāt
english: Cows, and gold, and sesame too have been extolled again and again, O tiger among men, on the strength of the Vedas' authority.

sanskrit: vivāhāṃś caiva kurvīta putrān utpādayeta ca putralābho hi kauravya sarvalābhād viśiṣyate
english: And one should make marriages and beget sons; for the gaining of a son, O descendant of Kuru, surpasses every other gain.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhūya eva kuruśreṣṭha dānānāṃ vidhim uttamam kathayasva mahāprājña bhūmidānaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Once again, O best of the Kurus, recount the supreme rule of gifts, O greatly wise one, and the gift of land in particular.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ kṣatriyo dadyād brāhmaṇas tāṃ svakarmaṇā vidhivat pratigṛhṇīyān na tv anyo dātum arhati
english: A kṣatriya should give land, and a brāhmaṇa by his own proper office should duly receive it; but no other has the right to give it.

sanskrit: sarvavarṇais tu yac chakyaṃ pradātuṃ phalakāṅkṣibhiḥ vede vā yat samāmnātaṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: What may be given by all the varṇas who long for its fruit, or what is enjoined in the Veda — that you ought to expound to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tulyanāmāni deyāni trīṇi tulyaphalāni ca sarvakāmaphalānīha gāvaḥ pṛthvī sarasvatī
english: Bhīṣma said: Three things to be given bear like names and like fruit, yielding here every desired reward — cows, the earth, and Sarasvatī (sacred speech).

sanskrit: yo brūyāc cāpi śiṣyāya dharmyāṃ brāhmīṃ sarasvatīm pṛthivīgopradānābhyāṃ sa tulyaṃ phalam aśnute
english: And he who would impart to a pupil the righteous, sacred speech of Brahman enjoys a fruit equal to the giving of land and cows.

sanskrit: tathaiva gāḥ praśaṃsanti na ca deyaṃ tataḥ param saṃnikṛṣṭaphalās tā hi laghvarthāś ca yudhiṣṭhira mātaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ sarvasukhapradāḥ
english: Likewise they praise cows, and nothing is to be given higher than they; for their fruit is close at hand and easily had, O Yudhiṣṭhira. Cows are the mothers of all beings, the bestowers of every happiness.

sanskrit: vṛddhim ākāṅkṣatā nityaṃ gāvaḥ kāryāḥ pradakṣiṇāḥ maṅgalāyatanaṃ devyas tasmāt pūjyāḥ sadaiva hi
english: He who longs for increase should ever keep cows and circle them to the right; these goddesses are the abode of auspiciousness, and therefore are ever to be revered.

sanskrit: pracodanaṃ devakṛtaṃ gavāṃ karmasu vartatām pūrvam evākṣaraṃ nānyad abhidheyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: For those engaged in the work of tending cows, a god-given impulse is at hand; only that first imperishable syllable, and nothing else, should ever be uttered over them.

sanskrit: pracāre vā nipāne vā budho nodvejayeta gāḥ tṛṣitā hy abhivīkṣantyo naraṃ hanyuḥ sabāndhavam
english: Whether at pasture or at the watering-trough, the wise man should not vex the cows; for thirsting and gazing upon him, they might destroy a man together with his kin.

sanskrit: pitṛsadmāni satataṃ devatāyatanāni ca pūyante śakṛtā yāsāṃ pūtaṃ kim adhikaṃ tataḥ
english: The dwellings of the fathers and the temples of the gods are forever purified by their dung — what is purer than that?

sanskrit: grāsamuṣṭiṃ paragave dadyāt saṃvatsaraṃ tu yaḥ akṛtvā svayam āhāraṃ vrataṃ tat sārvakāmikam
english: He who for a full year gives a handful of fodder to another's cow before he has taken his own food — that vow grants every desire.

sanskrit: sa hi putrān yaśorthaṃ ca śriyaṃ cāpy adhigacchati nāśayaty aśubhaṃ caiva duḥsvapnaṃ ca vyapohati
english: For he gains sons, and glory, and prosperity besides; he destroys what is inauspicious and drives away evil dreams.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca deyāḥ kiṃlakṣaṇā gāvaḥ kāś cāpi parivarjayet kīdṛśāya pradātavyā na deyāḥ kīdṛśāya ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what marks are the cows that should be given, and which should one avoid? To what kind of man should they be given, and to what kind not?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca asadvṛttāya pāpāya lubdhāyānṛtavādine havyakavyavyapetāya na deyā gauḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Bhīṣma said: To a man of evil conduct, a sinner, a greedy man, a speaker of falsehood, one who has forsaken the offerings to gods and ancestors — to such a one a cow should never in any way be given.

sanskrit: bhikṣave bahuputrāya śrotriyāyāhitāgnaye dattvā daśagavāṃ dātā lokān āpnoty anuttamān
english: But the giver who bestows ten cows upon a mendicant of many sons, a knower of the Veda who has kindled the sacred fire, attains the highest worlds.

sanskrit: yaṃ caiva dharmaṃ kurute tasya puṇyaphalaṃ ca yat sarvasyaivāṃśabhāg dātā tannimittaṃ pravṛttayaḥ
english: And of whatever dharma that man performs, and whatever the meritorious fruit thereof, the giver shares a portion of it all; for through him these undertakings come to be.

sanskrit: yaś cainam utpādayati yaś cainaṃ trāyate bhayāt yaś cāsya kurute vṛttiṃ sarve te pitaras trayaḥ
english: He who begets a man, he who saves him from danger, and he who provides his livelihood — these three are all his fathers.

sanskrit: kalmaṣaṃ guruśuśrūṣā hanti māno mahad yaśaḥ aputratāṃ trayaḥ putrā avṛttiṃ daśa dhenavaḥ
english: Service to one's elders destroys defilement; honor wins great fame; three sons remove childlessness, and ten milch-cows remove want of livelihood.

sanskrit: vedāntaniṣṭhasya bahuśrutasya; prajñānatṛptasya jitendriyasya śiṣṭasya dāntasya yatasya caiva; bhūteṣu nityaṃ priyavādinaś ca
english: To one steadfast in the end of the Veda, deeply learned, content in wisdom, his senses conquered, refined, self-restrained and disciplined, who speaks ever kindly to all beings —

sanskrit: yaḥ kṣudbhayād vai na vikarma kuryān; mṛdur dāntaś cātitheyaś ca nityam vṛttiṃ viprāyātisṛjeta tasmai; yas tulyaśīlaś ca saputradāraḥ
english: who out of fear of hunger would do no forbidden deed, who is gentle, self-controlled, and ever hospitable — to such a brāhmaṇa, of like virtue and with his sons and wife, one should grant a livelihood.

sanskrit: śubhe pātre ye guṇā gopradāne; tāvān doṣo brāhmaṇasvāpahāre sarvāvasthaṃ brāhmaṇasvāpahāro; dārāś caiṣāṃ dūrato varjanīyāḥ
english: As great as are the merits of giving a cow to a worthy recipient, so great is the sin in stealing a brāhmaṇa's property; in every circumstance the seizing of a brāhmaṇa's goods, and their wives as well, must be shunned from afar.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atraiva kīrtyate sadbhir brāhmaṇasvābhimarśane nṛgeṇa sumahat kṛcchraṃ yad avāptaṃ kurūdvaha
english: Bhīṣma said: On this very matter the good recount how, in laying hands upon a brāhmaṇa's property, the great distress was met by Nṛga, O foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: niviśantyāṃ purā pārtha dvāravatyām iti śrutiḥ adṛśyata mahākūpas tṛṇavīrutsamāvṛtaḥ
english: Long ago, as Dvāravatī was being settled, O Pārtha — so the tradition runs — a great well was found, overgrown with grass and creepers.

sanskrit: prayatnaṃ tatra kurvāṇās tasmāt kūpāj jalārthinaḥ śrameṇa mahatā yuktās tasmiṃs toye susaṃvṛte
english: Men in want of water, laboring there with great effort upon that well whose water was well concealed,

sanskrit: dadṛśus te mahākāyaṃ kṛkalāsam avasthitam tasya coddharaṇe yatnam akurvaṃs te sahasraśaḥ
english: saw a lizard of huge body lodged within; and they strove by the thousands to draw it out.

sanskrit: pragrahaiś carmapaṭṭaiś ca taṃ baddhvā parvatopamam nāśaknuvan samuddhartuṃ tato jagmur janārdanam
english: Binding it with ropes and straps of leather — that creature like a mountain — they could not haul it up; then they went to Janārdana.

sanskrit: kham āvṛtyodapānasya kṛkalāsaḥ sthito mahān tasya nāsti samuddhartety atha kṛṣṇe nyavedayan
english: "A great lizard sits blocking the mouth of the well, and there is no drawing it out" — so they reported to Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sa vāsudevena samuddhṛtaś ca; pṛṣṭaś ca kāmān nijagāda rājā nṛgas tadātmānam atho nyavedayat; purātanaṃ yajñasahasrayājinam
english: Drawn up by Vāsudeva, and asked of his desires, the king Nṛga then made himself known, declaring of old that he had offered a thousand sacrifices.

sanskrit: tathā bruvāṇaṃ tu tam āha mādhavaḥ; śubhaṃ tvayā karma kṛtaṃ na pāpakam kathaṃ bhavān durgatim īdṛśīṃ gato; narendra tad brūhi kim etad īdṛśam
english: To him speaking thus Mādhava said: "Pure was the deed you did, and not sinful; how then did you come to so wretched a state, O lord of men? Tell me — what is this thing of such a kind?"

sanskrit: śataṃ sahasrāṇi śataṃ gavāṃ punaḥ; punaḥ śatāny aṣṭa śatāyutāni tvayā purā dattam itīha śuśruma; nṛpa dvijebhyaḥ kva nu tad gataṃ tava
english: "A hundred thousand cows, a hundred again and again, eight hundred myriads — so we have heard that you of old gave to the twice-born, O king. Where then has that merit of yours gone?"

sanskrit: nṛgas tato 'bravīt kṛṣṇaṃ brāhmaṇasyāgnihotriṇaḥ proṣitasya paribhraṣṭā gaur ekā mama godhane
english: Then Nṛga said to Kṛṣṇa: "A single cow belonging to a brāhmaṇa, a keeper of the sacred fire who was away from home, had strayed into my herd of cattle.

sanskrit: gavāṃ sahasre saṃkhyātā tadā sā paśupair mama sā brāhmaṇāya me dattā pretyārtham abhikāṅkṣatā
english: Counted then by my herdsmen among a thousand cows, she was given by me to a brāhmaṇa, for I sought reward in the world beyond.

sanskrit: apaśyat parimārgaṃś ca tāṃ yāṃ paragṛhe dvijaḥ mameyam iti covāca brāhmaṇo yasya sābhavat
english: And the brāhmaṇa whose she had been, searching, spied her in another's house, and said, 'This cow is mine.'

sanskrit: tāv ubhau samanuprāptau vivadantau bhṛśajvarau bhavān dātā bhavān hartety atha tau māṃ tadocatuḥ
english: The two of them came before me, disputing in great heat, and they said to me then: 'You are the giver — you are the thief!'

sanskrit: śatena śatasaṃkhyena gavāṃ vinimayena vai yāce pratigrahītāraṃ sa tu mām abravīd idam
english: With an exchange of a hundred cows by the hundred I begged the one who had received her; but he said this to me:

sanskrit: deśakālopasaṃpannā dogdhrī kṣāntātivatsalā svādukṣīrapradā dhanyā mama nityaṃ niveśane
english: 'She is suited to time and place, a good milker, gentle, most loving, a giver of sweet milk, auspicious, and ever in my home.

sanskrit: kṛśaṃ ca bharate yā gaur mama putram apastanam na sā śakyā mayā hātum ity uktvā sa jagāma ha
english: And this cow nourishes my frail, unweaned son; her I cannot give up.' Having spoken thus, he went away.

sanskrit: tatas tam aparaṃ vipraṃ yāce vinimayena vai gavāṃ śatasahasraṃ vai tatkṛte gṛhyatām iti
english: Then I begged that other brāhmaṇa in exchange: 'Let a hundred thousand cows be taken in her stead.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca na rājñāṃ pratigṛhṇāmi śakto 'haṃ svasya mārgaṇe saiva gaur dīyatāṃ śīghraṃ mameti madhusūdana
english: The brāhmaṇa said: 'I accept nothing from kings; I am able to seek out my own. Let that very cow be given back to me at once' — so he said, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: rukmam aśvāṃś ca dadato rajataṃ syandanāṃs tathā na jagrāha yayau cāpi tadā sa brāhmaṇarṣabhaḥ
english: Though I offered gold and horses, silver and chariots too, that bull among brāhmaṇas would take none of it, and then went his way.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu coditaḥ kāladharmaṇā pitṛlokam ahaṃ prāpya dharmarājam upāgamam
english: At that very time, urged on by the law of Time, I reached the world of the fathers and came before the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: yamas tu pūjayitvā māṃ tato vacanam abravīt nāntaḥ saṃkhyāyate rājaṃs tava puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ
english: Yama, having honored me, then spoke these words: 'No end can be reckoned, O king, to your meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: asti caiva kṛtaṃ pāpam ajñānāt tad api tvayā carasva pāpaṃ paścād vā pūrvaṃ vā tvaṃ yathecchasi
english: And yet a sin too has been committed — and that by you in ignorance. Undergo the penalty for that sin either afterward or before, as you please.'"
